set_aside: v. 10, Ma'avar Yabbok (Siftei Tzedek): שומר בריתו, "keeps his covenant" (sexual purity), is an idiom, not this psalm.
v. 13, Seder Ma'amadot: מַיִם. כְּמוֹ are only adjacent words ("waters, as it is written"), a coincidence.
v. 19, Ma'avar Yabbok (Author's Introduction): לערוך שלחן, "to set a table" for the God-fearing, is an idiom, not the psalm's taunt.
v. 37, blessing on seeing a rainbow (Ashkenaz siddur): נֶאֱמָן בִּבְרִיתוֹ describes God's faithfulness to the covenant of Noah, an idiom, not this psalm.
v. 37, blessing on seeing a rainbow (Sefard siddur): the same idiom.
v. 37, blessing on seeing a rainbow (Edot HaMizrach siddur): the same idiom.

v. 70, Avodah Service, Yom Kippur Musaf (Ashkenaz and Sefard machzorim): מִמִּכְלְאוֹת צֹאן עֲדָרִים דָּלְלוּ belongs to a catalogue of crop failures modelled on Habakkuk 3:17, not David taken from the sheepfolds.
